note: Holdout set for task G (2026-11-28), written after the first Gemini Nano run without looking at its output and never used for tuning. Same conventions as eval/task_g.json: phone-domain signs are not rules (cfg.phone.enabled is false), late phone use counts as a later rest midpoint, items and actions by meaning (counted), rules scored exactly. Only summary numbers may be read while tuning a prompt; the evaluation screen hides its per-case table.

cases.text:
Signs:
- up past 1am most nights
- skipping band practice
- cereal for dinner
Helps:
- texting my best friend
- a cold shower
Going to the gym really helps me, and so does seeing my cousin. When it starts I sleep ten or eleven hours and I stop answering emails.
I still go to work every day, that never changes, but I stop leaving the house at weekends and I go to bed much later.
My girlfriend notices it before I do: I stop going to the climbing hall, I hardly walk anywhere and I don't call my parents anymore. Cooking together helps.
Weirdly I go to bed at eight and wake up at four. I also stop going to church on Sunday. A chat with the pastor helps.
I walk more slowly and everything takes longer. I stop shaving. My dog makes me go out.
My usual weekly routine falls apart. Planning my week on Sunday helps.
I end up going to fewer and fewer places. I also stop washing my hair. Meeting a friend at a café helps.
actions: meet a friend at a café

cases.text: Things just feel heavy and I don't really know why.
I haven't figured out my warning signs. Gardening, podcasts and my sister's cooking help.
My watch shows my heart rate variability dropping, and I go to bed later and later. Yoga helps.
i stop going to college, sleep wayy less and dont eat breakfst. talking to my tutor helps
You notice you stay in your flat all day and you stop going to choir. Calling your brother helps.
I stop brushing my teeth, stop paying bills, stop replying to my group chat and I go to bed really late. Making a small list helps.

It's not one thing. Work is busy, my landlord is annoying, and the weather doesn't help, but that's life. What I do notice, looking back at the last two times, is that I stop going to my running club, then I spend whole weekends indoors, and my sleep times get completely irregular, some nights at ten, some at three. I also stop seeing my friends. What helps most is a walk with my neighbour and putting my phone in another room in the evening.
If I start missing football training and stop moving much during the day, that's the sign. Listening to old music helps.
Last time it began with me staying in bed until eleven every day and not going to the library to study anymore. My mentor checking in helped.
I sleep so much more, like twelve hours, and I hardly go outside. Fresh air helps.
My days stop having any rhythm, I eat at random times and nap whenever. A fixed lunch time helps.
I'm on my phone until 3am and I stop going to the office. Leaving my phone in the kitchen helps.

1. bed after midnight
2. no more swimming pool
3. no walks
What helps: my niece visiting.
Less walking, staying in more.
I avoid my friends, I don't answer the door and I stop texting back. Seeing my therapist helps.
I feel empty and tired, and I stop going to my evening class. Talking to my flatmate helps.
I stop going to work and to the gym, and I sleep in until the afternoon. A morning alarm across the room helps.
My resting heart rate doesn't change, but I go to fewer places and walk less. Calling my aunt helps.
Am I going to bed later? Am I skipping the pottery studio? Those are my signs. Making something with my hands helps.
When it gets bad I stop going to my volleyball club and I basically live on my couch. Fietsen helps, honestly.
My bedtime moves around a lot and I stop going to the market on Saturdays. Baking bread helps.
I sleep much less than usual and I stop leaving my room. Breathing exercises help.
